lesson: English that works at work (A2 · Aula 0)

cards.definition: The last day or time when something must be finished.
cards.example:
- The deadline is Friday, so I need your part by Thursday.
O prazo é sexta, então preciso da sua parte até quinta.
cards.note: Meet a deadline (cumprir) x miss a deadline (perder).

cards.definition: A time when people come together to talk about work.
cards.example:
- We have a short meeting every Monday to organize the week.
Temos uma reunião curta toda segunda para organizar a semana.
cards.note: Have/attend a meeting; set up a meeting = marcar.

cards.definition: A document with information about work that was done.
cards.example:
- I send the sales report to my manager every Friday.
Envio o relatório de vendas para minha gestora toda sexta.
cards.note: Write/send a report. Como verbo: report to = ser subordinado a.

cards.definition: A person or company that pays you for a service.
cards.example:
- Our biggest client is in Portugal, so we speak English every day.
Nosso maior cliente é de Portugal, então falamos inglês todos os dias.

cards.definition: Having a lot to do and no free time.
cards.example:
- I'm busy until three, but I'm free after that.
Estou ocupado até as três, mas fico livre depois disso.
cards.note: Busy WITH algo; a busy week = uma semana cheia.

cards.definition: Finished and prepared to be used or shown.
cards.example:
- The presentation is almost ready — I just need the numbers.
A apresentação está quase pronta — só faltam os números.
cards.note: Be ready FOR algo ou ready TO + verbo.

cards.definition: A polite way to ask someone to send you something.
cards.example:
- Could you send me the file before the meeting, please?
Você poderia me enviar o arquivo antes da reunião, por favor?
cards.note: Fórmula educada universal: Could you + verbo. Muito melhor que “Send me”.

cards.translation: eu te retorno / eu te dou um retorno
cards.definition: Used to say you will answer later, when you have the information.
cards.example:
- I don't have the answer now — I'll get back to you today.
Não tenho a resposta agora — eu te retorno hoje.
cards.note: Salva qualquer situação em que você não sabe a resposta na hora.

cards.definition: To go to a meeting, class or event.
cards.example:
- I attend the weekly meeting, and I answer the phone when my colleague is out.
Participo da reunião semanal e atendo o telefone quando meu colega não está.
cards.note: “Atender o telefone” é answer the phone — nunca attend.

cards.definition: Used to correct information or give a surprising fact.
cards.example:
- Actually, I prefer emails: I have time to think in English.
Na verdade, eu prefiro e-mails: tenho tempo de pensar em inglês.
cards.note: “Atualmente” é currently. Actually corrige uma impressão.

exercise.title: English that works at work (A2 · Aula 0)

questions.prompt: The _____ is Friday, so I need your part by Thursday.
Every Monday the team talks about the week. They have a…
questions.explanation: You HAVE a meeting — “make a meeting” is the Portuguese “fazer”.

questions.prompt: Eu mando o relatório de vendas toda sexta.
questions.answer: I send the sales report every Friday.|I send the sales report on Fridays.
questions.explanation: “Report” is the document; it is also the verb “to report”.

questions.prompt: Our biggest _____ is in Portugal, so we speak English every day.
questions.explanation: “Client” pays for a service; “customer” buys a product.

questions.prompt: Estou ocupado até as três, mas depois estou livre.
questions.answer: I'm busy until three, but I'm free after that.|I am busy until three, but I am free after that.

questions.prompt: The presentation is almost _____ — I just need the numbers.
You want the file before the meeting. The polite way is:
options: Could you send me the file?
questions.answer: Could you send me the file?
questions.explanation: “Could you…?” turns an order into a request.

questions.prompt: I don't have the answer now — _____ today.
questions.explanation: “Get back to you” means to answer later.

questions.prompt: You go to the weekly meeting. You…
questions.explanation: “Attend” means to go to. The Portuguese “assistir” tempts “assist”, which means to help.

questions.prompt: Your colleague says the report is due today, but it is due tomorrow. You say:
questions.explanation: “Actually” corrects information. It is not “atualmente”, which is “currently”.
